title: feat(edm): 2-axis wire contour op - kerf offset to a stated punch/die side, start hole, corner refusal
body:
**Stacked on #560 (on #551) - this diff shows their commits until they merge; merge #551, #560 first.** This PR adds three commits on top of #560's head (`f5d8c06a`) and two merges of `origin/main` (no conflicts). Not exercised on a real EDM control.

## What changed

The first wire EDM operation (#532, part of #290; decisions D1, D2, D4, D8): **Wire Contour**, a vertical cut of one closed profile.

**Generator** - `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/` (beside the other 2D generators, on the existing offsetter):
- The wire-centre path is the profile's parallel at the **kerf offset = wire radius + the condition's spark gap**, on the **stated** side: inside the profile for a `die`, outside it for a `punch`. The side is never inferred.
- A straight lead-in runs from the stated **start hole / threading point** to the nearest point of the path; the profile is cut counter-clockwise; the lead-out retraces the lead-in.
- **Corner minimum:** an inside corner, slot, notch or neck the wire cannot cut (tighter than wire radius + gap) is refused by name with its spot and the minimum radius. Outside corners are mitred, so the wire never comes nearer than the offset.
- Refused by name, never trimmed: no start hole, a start hole on the product's side or nearer than the offset, an open profile, several profiles, a crossing or area-less ring, a profile smaller than the wire.
- The moves ride the lower programmed plane and state **no pose and no feed** (D2: it posts as XY; the control's generator sets the rate).

**Operation** - `crates/app`:
- `OpType::WireContour` (stored id 41, appended), its own **Wire EDM** section and family, admitted on a `wire_edm` machine only.
- Created and edited through `CreateOperation` / `EditOperationParams` (also paste and retype). At the command door, **a missing condition, gap or wire diameter is refused by name** through #531's `Edm::condition`.
- **A wire cut mounts no library tool.** Its wire diameter and gap come from the machine's condition table, their only source; a wire cut that names a tool is refused. The stamp digests the condition, so an edited table re-marks the cut Stale.
- The machine check on a wire EDM judges X/Y travel and names what it does not judge. The program gate refuses a wire cut by name until a wire post exists (#533).
- The op rides the project file (`wire_contour { top_z, bottom_z, condition, side, start }`). `side` has no default: a file or patch without it is refused.

`crates/ui` gains the match arms the new kind forces and a **minimal page** (`wire_page.rs`: side and start hole on Geometry, the two planes on Heights, the machine's conditions to choose from on Passes; no Feeds tab) - the UI's registry-wide tab law fails a kind whose tabs draw nothing. The ribbon's quick-add names no tool for a kind that mounts none, and its tip names a wire EDM as the machine wire work needs. No new icon; the real page, viewport picking of the start hole and the ribbon on a wire EDM document are #535.

Decisions the umbrella left open are in `docs/decisions/532-wire-contour.md` (no library tool, mitred outside corners, the 2 um cover tolerance, no arc fitting, lead shape, where each refusal stands, no CL format change).

## Readings

Synthetic condition `C110` (from no machine's manual): wire 0.250 mm, gap 0.040 mm. Profile: 40 x 20 mm, 2 mm corners in 3-degree facets.

| | wire-centre path, top side | distance to the profile |
|---|---|---|
| die | y = 9.835 | 0.165 inside |
| punch | y = 10.165 | 0.165 outside |
| apart | 0.330 | = kerf width (0.25 + 2 x 0.04) |

- On the straight sides the paths stand at the offset to 1e-9 mm in the motion test and 1e-6 mm through the commands (the model's silhouette in between). The nearest any path vertex comes to the profile is the offset to 1e-6 mm; the farthest is under 0.2 um past it (a 3-degree facet's mitre).
- A sharp 40 x 20 rectangle as a die: refused, "minimum inside radius is 0.1650 mm (wire radius 0.1250 + spark gap 0.0400)". The same rectangle as a punch: cut, with sharp path corners at (20.165, 10.165). A 0.1 mm fillet as a die: refused; a 0.2 mm fillet: cut.

## How tested

- `camcraft-motion` lib, `wire_edm::tests` (5): `a_die_and_a_punch_on_one_profile_stand_apart_by_exactly_the_kerf`, `a_corner_tighter_than_the_wire_is_refused_by_name`, `a_missing_or_misplaced_start_hole_is_refused_by_name`, `degenerate_profiles_and_numbers_are_refused_by_name`, `the_moves_ride_one_plane_with_no_pose_from_and_to_the_start_hole`.
- `camcraft-app` `wire_contour` (7): the family door both ways and no tool; the condition door at creation and edit; die and punch apart by the kerf through the commands, the machine check and the post's refusal; the corner and start-hole refusals at generation; the stamp reading the condition; undo / redo; the project round trip and the undefaulted side.
- `golden_cl`: `wire_contour_die_and_punch_match_golden` with `tests/golden/wire_contour_die.cl` and `wire_contour_punch.cl` (LF).
- `tool_law`: `every_kind_names_a_tool_set` now states the one exception (the wire family mounts none).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on the final head `13a12a25`: **green** - post, motion (195 passed), app (the whole suite, 285 test results, because a golden changed), ui (lib and 7 suites). The parents' `edm_machine` (7) and `edm_conditions` (6), `operations` (117) and `golden_cl` (26) are in that run.
- The first gate run was red: three registry pins (the kind count, two ribbon rows), the empty-rack tool refusal test, the UI tab law and the UI tip table. All were the new kind meeting laws that walk every kind; fixed in `cded9490`, and the second run is the green one.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- **Not exercised on a real EDM control.** The condition is synthetic; nothing here was cut.
- No wire post exists (#533), so no NC was written; the program gate refuses a wire cut by name.
- No verification of the wire against the part, the slug or the start hole's clearance (#534). The generator certifies only its own two laws (no move nearer the profile than the offset; no profile point the kerf misses).
- The page was only drawn by the registry-wide tab law test (every tab draws, one tab per field); no test clicks through it, and it was not looked at in the running app. On a wire EDM document the ribbon's Wire Contour cell creates a draft that the door refuses until a condition is named, and with an empty tool library the cell is disabled ("No tool yet") although the kind needs none - both #535.
- A picked-edge profile (a selection source) is wired the way the plasma profile's is but was only tested from a whole model's silhouette.
- A wire cut on a setup with an aligned part, carried stock or fixtures was not tested.

## Follow-ups filed

- #1108 `MCP: wire contour op` - `add_operation` requires a non-empty `tool`, and no headless way mounts a wire EDM with conditions yet, so the op is not reachable over MCP in this PR.
- #1109 open-profile contour (a cut-off or slot from the stock edge) - refused by name here.
- #1110 program sim, setup sheet and tool list still read a wire cut's empty tool name.

Changelog: Wire EDM: a Wire Contour operation cuts one closed profile at the kerf offset of the machine's condition (wire radius + spark gap), on a stated die or punch side, from a stated start hole; a corner the wire cannot cut and a missing start hole are refused by name (#532)

Effort: max (not escalated)

Fixes #532
